title: Finite morphisms are quasi-finite
statement:
A finite morphism of
schemes is quasi-finite.

proof.text: Let $f$ be a finite morphism. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $f$ is proper, hence of finite type; by the definition of finite type recorded in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $f$ is therefore quasi-compact and locally of finite type. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], every fibre $f^{-1}(\{y\})$ is finite. Applying the reverse implication of [pqf-lem-qf-finitefibres] gives that $f$ is quasi-finite.
